# Multi-Format File Viewer Chrome Extension

> **Code location:** `/Volumes/D/www/projects/khanakia/chrome-extensions/filemark/` — this dir holds planning docs only. Project name is **filemark**; npm scope is **`@filemark/*`**. Monorepo already scaffolded (pnpm workspaces, tsup, React 19) with `apps/chrome-ext`, `packages/viewer-core` (`@filemark/core`), `packages/mdx-viewer` (`@filemark/mdx`), `packages/json-viewer`, `packages/schema-viewer`.

> Private problem doc + quick plan. Lives outside the public repo on purpose. v0.1 ships markdown-only. Architecture is multi-format from day one (pluggable renderer registry + per-viewer packages) so JSON / code / CSV / images can land in v0.2+ without rework — and the markdown viewer itself is reusable as an npm package in a future VS Code extension or standalone React app.

## Problem

No Chrome extension offers a **good** in-browser viewing experience for the text files a developer / writer touches daily — markdown, MDX, JSON, JSONC, TS/TSX, YAML, CSV, logs, images. Existing options are either:

- **Too basic** — drag a `.md` or `.json` file in, get rendered HTML or an unstyled tree. No persistence, no organization, no interactivity.
- **Too dev-ish** — assume you're viewing raw GitHub files, not using these formats as a daily reading / reference surface.
- **Format-siloed** — one extension for markdown, another for JSON, another for CSV. No shared library, no unified search, no shared theming.
- **Abandoned** — most haven't been updated in 3+ years, broken on MV3, or bloated with ads.

### What hurts day-to-day

1. **No library / bookmarking** — every file is a one-off drop. Can't star, favorite, or come back to it.
2. **No folder organization** — can't group files into projects, topics, tags regardless of type.
3. **No interactive components** — markdown checkboxes don't toggle, JSON trees don't fold, CSV has no filter, code has no jump-to-symbol.
4. **No persistence** — refresh = lose the view. Re-drag the file every time.
5. **No local folder watching** — `mydocs/` or `myrepo/` full of mixed files. Want to browse it like a mini-Obsidian / VS Code preview in the browser without installing another desktop app.
6. **No cross-format search** — full-text over md, JSON values, code, logs, all at once.
7. **No TOC / outline** — long docs and deep JSON are a wall of text.
8. **No theming** — stuck on white, light grey, or black. No typography control. Code blocks don't match the rest of the UI.

### Trigger

Every time I drop a local `.md`, `.json`, or `.tsx` into Chrome to read it. Multiple times a day. Each re-load is a small paper cut, and the lack of org means I rebuild context every single time.

### Current workaround

- VS Code preview pane (heavy, context-switch)
- Obsidian (markdown only, overkill, separate vault per topic)
- `jq` / `cat` / `bat` in terminal (not sharable, no library)
- GitHub gist (requires upload, not private by default)
- Just reading raw text (tiring)

### Target impact

- **High** — multi-times-a-day friction, long horizon (these formats are forever)
- **Time saved:** ~10-20 min/day across context switches + re-opens
- **Frustration:** very high; current options all compromise something

## Quick Plan

### Core value prop

> "The universal file browser for Chrome." Drop files or point at a folder. Renders markdown beautifully, JSON as a tree, code with syntax highlight, CSV as a filterable table — all in one app. It remembers them. Bookmark, organize, search across every format. No account, no cloud, all local.

### Supported file types (launch set)

| Extension | Renderer | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.md` | MDX pipeline | GFM, tables, task lists |
| `.mdx` | MDX pipeline | JSX components (sandboxed for non-local sources) |
| `.json`, `.jsonc` | Tree viewer + raw tab | Virtualized for large files |
| `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx` | Shiki code viewer | Fold, copy, line links |
| `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.toml` | Shiki code viewer | |
| `.css`, `.scss`, `.html` | Shiki code viewer | |
| `.csv`, `.tsv` | Table viewer | Sticky header, filter, sort |
| `.log`, `.txt` | Monospace viewer | Grep / highlight box |
| `.diff`, `.patch` | Shiki diff grammar | |
| `.svg`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.webp` | Image viewer | Zoom, pan |
| (unknown) | Fallback: Shiki auto-detect or plain text | |

v0.2+: `.ipynb`, `.sqlite`, `.parquet` (sample), `.xml`, `.geojson` map view.

### Core architecture

**Monorepo** (pnpm workspaces). Each viewer is a self-contained package with zero host-platform imports (no `chrome.*`, no `vscode.*`, no Node `fs`). Host-specific concerns — storage, asset resolution, theming, navigation — are injected via props / context using interfaces defined in `viewer-core`. Goal: the same `@viewers/mdx` package drops into the Chrome ext today, a VS Code webview tomorrow, and a standalone React app later with no rewrite.

```
repo/
├── apps/
│   ├── chrome-ext/          MV3 shell, consumes @viewers/*
│   ├── vscode-ext/          (future) webview shell
│   └── web-demo/            (future) standalone React app
├── packages/
│   ├── viewer-core/         shared: Renderer interface, types, ThemeProvider, adapter interfaces
│   ├── mdx-viewer/          @viewers/mdx — v0.1 target
│   ├── json-viewer/         (v0.2+)
│   ├── code-viewer/         (v0.2+)
│   ├── csv-viewer/          (v0.2+)
│   └── image-viewer/        (v0.2+)
└── pnpm-workspace.yaml
```

**Renderer registry** (lives in the host app, not in packages) keyed by file extension:

```ts
import { MDXViewer } from "@viewers/mdx";
// v0.2+: import { JSONViewer } from "@viewers/json"; ...

const registry: Record<string, Renderer> = {
  md: MDXViewer,
  mdx: MDXViewer,
  // v0.2+ extensions plug in here; no viewer-core changes required
};
```

**Package portability rules** (enforced in CI via lint rule + boundary test):

- No `chrome.*`, no `vscode.*`, no Node built-ins.
- Peer deps: `react`, `react-dom`. Everything else bundled or declared as normal dep.
- Each package ships its own build (tsup or vite lib mode), its own types, its own `package.json` with a scoped name.
- Host-specific concerns injected via props:

  ```ts
  // packages/viewer-core/src/types.ts
  export interface StorageAdapter {
    get(key: string): Promise<unknown>;
    set(key: string, value: unknown): Promise<void>;
  }
  export interface AssetResolver {
    resolve(relativePath: string): Promise<string>; // returns blob: or https: URL
  }
  export interface ViewerProps {
    content: string;
    sourceUrl?: string;
    assets?: AssetResolver;
    storage?: StorageAdapter;
    onNavigate?: (href: string) => void;
  }
  ```

Host wiring: Chrome ext → IndexedDB-backed storage + FSA-backed assets. VS Code ext → `workspace.fs`-backed. Web demo → `localStorage` + `fetch`.

Shared **library shell** (sidebar, tags, search, theming) lives in `apps/chrome-ext/` — it is not part of the portable viewer packages. VS Code ext will reuse the viewer package but build its own host shell around it.

### MVP scope (v0.1 — markdown only)

v0.1 ships **only `.md` and `.mdx`**. The monorepo and renderer registry exist from day one so v0.2+ formats slot in without re-architecting, but no other viewer packages are built yet.

1. **File ingest (`.md` / `.mdx` only)**
   - Drag & drop one or many files
   - File System Access API → pick a local folder, read all `.md` / `.mdx` recursively
   - Persist file handles via IndexedDB (permission auto-restored in MV3)
2. **Library view**
   - Sidebar with folder tree + flat list
   - Star / pin files
   - Last-opened list
3. **Render view — `@viewers/mdx`**
   - `@mdx-js/mdx` + `remark-gfm` + `rehype-katex` + Mermaid
   - Shiki syntax highlighting for fenced code blocks
   - Built-in components: `<Callout>`, `<Tabs>`, `<Details>`
   - Task-list checkboxes that **toggle & persist** (via injected `StorageAdapter`)
   - Auto TOC + collapsible headings
4. **Organization**
   - Tags on files (stored locally, not in the file)
   - Virtual folders / collections
5. **Search**
   - Full-text over all loaded `.md` / `.mdx` files (FlexSearch or MiniSearch)
   - Filter by tag
6. **Theming**
   - Light / dark / sepia
   - Font, width, line-height controls
   - Shiki theme shared between Markdown code blocks and (later) the code viewer

### v0.2+ — additional format packages (good-to-have)

Each lands as its own package under `packages/`, registered in `apps/chrome-ext/` via the renderer registry. Order TBD by demand:

- `@viewers/json` — `.json`, `.jsonc` → virtualized tree + raw tab + jq-lite filter box
- `@viewers/code` — `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.css`, `.html` → Shiki highlight, copy, fold, line anchors, wrap toggle, `.diff` / `.patch` support
- `@viewers/csv` — `.csv`, `.tsv` → table, filter, sort, column toggle
- `@viewers/image` — `.svg`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.webp` → zoom, pan
- `@viewers/log` — `.log`, `.txt` → monospace + grep / highlight box

### Further stretch (v0.3+)

- VS Code extension consuming `@viewers/mdx` in a webview (first external consumer → validates portability)
- Standalone web demo at e.g. `viewer.dev` consuming the same packages
- Live reload when underlying file changes
- Edit mode (Monaco or CodeMirror) — gated per-format
- Export loaded folder → single HTML bundle
- Sync bookmarks/tags across Chrome profiles via `chrome.storage.sync`
- Link graph (backlinks between `.md` files + JSON `$ref` graph)
- `.ipynb` renderer
- Diff two files of the same type
- Search inside JSON values, code symbols, CSV cells — not just raw text

### Tech stack (draft)

| Concern | Pick | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Monorepo | pnpm workspaces | Lightweight, good peer-dep handling |
| Package build | tsup (or vite lib mode) | Fast ESM/CJS + types for publishable packages |
| Manifest | MV3 | Required for Chrome Web Store |
| Host app | React + TypeScript + Vite + CRXJS | Fast HMR, small bundle |
| Markdown / MDX | `@mdx-js/mdx` + `remark-gfm` + `rehype-katex` + Mermaid | JSX components in docs, powerful |
| Code highlight | Shiki | Shared across MD code blocks and (v0.2+) code viewer |
| JSON tree (v0.2+) | `react-json-view-lite` or custom virtualized tree | Handles big files |
| CSV (v0.2+) | Papaparse + TanStack Table | |
| Storage | IndexedDB via `idb-keyval` (Chrome host) | FS handles + metadata |
| Search | FlexSearch | Small, fast, local |
| Styling | Tailwind v4 + CSS vars | Theming cheap; CSS vars let packages be theme-agnostic |

### Open questions

- [ ] **Name** — old name (`markdown-viewer-chrome-ext`) is wrong once v0.2 adds more formats. Candidates: `fileview`, `viewly`, `lumen`, `snip`, `readly`. Pick before scaffolding. Repo name, Chrome Web Store name, and npm scope (e.g. `@viewly/mdx`) should align.
- [ ] **npm scope** — `@viewers/*`, `@<chosen-name>/*`, or unscoped? Affects package imports forever.
- [ ] Sidepanel API vs full tab UI vs both? (Sidepanel = always-on reading pane, tab = spacious library)
- [ ] Local folder reads on every Chrome start — user has to re-grant? Verify MV3 persistence of FSA handles.
- [ ] How to handle images referenced as relative paths in local `.md` files? (blob URL mapping via the injected `AssetResolver`)
- [ ] **MDX security** — MDX executes JSX. Local / folder-granted files = trusted. Remote `.mdx` fetched via URL interception = risky. Options: (a) sandbox remote MDX in iframe w/ strict CSP; (b) refuse to evaluate JSX for non-local sources, degrade to plain md; (c) allow-list origins. This decision lives inside `@viewers/mdx` (via a `trust: "full" | "safe"` prop) so every host picks its own policy.
- [ ] **URL interception scope** — file:// only, or also raw.githubusercontent, gist raw, *.md served as text/plain? More coverage = more perms.
- [ ] Monetization? Free + optional paid sync? Or purely free / open-source?

### Milestones

1. **Week 1** — rename repo; scaffold pnpm monorepo (`apps/chrome-ext`, `packages/viewer-core`, `packages/mdx-viewer`); scaffold MV3 host (Vite + CRXJS + React + TS); renderer registry stub; drag-drop single file → empty viewer.
2. **Week 2** — build `@viewers/mdx`: MDX pipeline + Shiki + KaTeX + Mermaid + built-in components; render one `.md` file end-to-end.
3. **Week 3** — File System Access API, persist handles, folder tree sidebar, last-opened list, file-type icons.
4. **Week 4** — search + tags + bookmarking; theming (light/dark/sepia + typography); TOC; task-list persistence via injected `StorageAdapter` → v0.1 private test.
5. **Week 5+** — polish, MDX security posture, Chrome Web Store listing.
6. **v0.2+** — add `@viewers/json`, `@viewers/code`, etc. one package at a time; publish `@viewers/mdx` to npm once API is stable.
7. **v0.3+** — VS Code extension webview consuming `@viewers/mdx` (first external consumer → validates the portability claim).

### Success metrics

- **v0.1:** I personally replace VS Code preview + Obsidian (for markdown reading) within 2 weeks of shipping
- Can open a `.md`-heavy folder and browse without re-dragging
- Task-list checkboxes persist across reloads
- Sub-100ms search on 500+ markdown files
- **Portability proof:** `@viewers/mdx` imports and renders correctly in a bare `create-vite` React app with zero code changes (run as a local sanity check before v0.1 ship)
- **v0.3:** same package boots inside a VS Code webview

## Status

- **Date opened:** 2026-04-19
- **Last updated:** 2026-04-21 (scope expanded markdown → multi-format)
- **Status:** planning
- **Next step:** pick name + npm scope → scaffold pnpm monorepo (`apps/chrome-ext`, `packages/viewer-core`, `packages/mdx-viewer`)
